want.name: Sports · single player props
fit: a single objective prop settles cleanly as a binary/bracket
captured: sports binaries live on Kalshi; single-prop breadth thin vs sportsbooks' hundreds
want.sentence: Bettors use sportsbooks for player props; a binary fits a single objective prop, but the book wins the breadth because it IS the counterparty — a market needs two-sided liquidity in each of thousands of thin props; blocker = per-market liquidity / tail fragmentation (hard); proof = deep books across prop breadth, not just star-player headliners.

want.name: Sports · same-game parlays
demand: SGP is most of the props+SGP handle and ~40% of online revenue
fit: independent binaries cannot price leg correlation, but a combination listed as ONE contract prices it — an event venue trades a sports combinatorial book; how much SGP demand that form serves is unproven
captured: no predmarket replicates correlated SGP pricing
want.sentence: Bettors use sportsbooks for SGPs; independent binaries can't price leg correlation, but a combo listed as one contract can, and an event venue now trades one; blocker = correlation (structural); proof = an event-venue SGP book sustaining volume.

want.name: Crypto perp
fit: the perp IS the native crypto leverage form
want.sentence: Crypto traders already use perps for leveraged direction; the form won; residual = long-tail token breadth + execution; blocker = tail liquidity (solvable); proof = new-listing depth/OI.

want.name: Equity perp
demand: ~15.2B US option contracts/yr (OCC) + lev/inverse ETFs — observable
fit: serves linear directional leverage; NOT convexity / defined-risk / income / hedging (most options flow)
captured: on-chain equity perp tiny; HIP-3 / Ostium nascent — not migrating
want.sentence: Retail uses options/CFDs/lev-ETFs for leveraged equity direction; a perp wins on simple linear leverage (no greeks, 24/7) but fails for convexity/defined-risk/income; blocker = US regulation (hard) + liquidity (solvable); proof = an equity perp sustaining open interest.

want.name: Commodity perp
demand: commodity ETFs + retail futures — observable, mid-size
fit: a perp fits directional commodity exposure
captured: Ostium / HL commodity live, small — not strongly migrating
want.sentence: Retail uses commodity ETFs/futures for directional metals/energy; a perp wins on 24/7 leverage + access; demand is plausible but not yet revealing on-chain; blocker = liquidity / pro supply (solvable); proof = sustained commodity-perp OI beyond gold.

want.name: FX perp (majors)
demand: major-FX retail directional appetite is low — low realized vol
want.sentence: Retail can trade major FX via CFDs but appetite is thin (low vol = no excitement); the wrapper is fine, the demand isn't; blocker = low volatility (structural); proof = none on majors (watch high-vol EM/exotic only).

want.name: Pre-IPO perp
demand: private-secondary ~$3-12B/yr (Forge et al.); Ventuals proved ~$650M traded before wind-down
fit: the perp is the only form serving pre-IPO exposure — but single-name has no live external mark (M-weak; Ventuals settled OpenAI/Anthropic at internal-orderbook TWAP)
captured: Ventuals wound down Jun'26 (team → another HL build); trade.xyz remains — venue consolidation, not demand failure
want.sentence: Investors use private secondaries for pre-IPO exposure; a perp wins on access + liquidity but real share/name supply is scarce AND single-name has no live external mark (Ventuals TWAP-settled at wind-down, then was absorbed — pioneer, not moat); blocker = name supply (hard); proof = a multi-name pre-IPO perp with real OI.

want.name: Rates perp
demand: retail rates-directional is thin; expressed via Treasury ETFs
fit: a perp works but retail prefers the ETF wrapper
want.sentence: Retail expresses rates views via Treasury/lev-Treasury ETFs; a perp adds little and the directional want is thin; blocker = weak retail want (structural); proof = none expected.

want.name: Crypto funding-rate future (Boros)
demand: funding exposure on ~$175-220B perp OI; ~$17-22B immediately tokenizable, ~$150B full pool; users (Ethena, basis funds) already on-chain & funding-exposed
fit: a funding-rate future is the native form for trading a previously-embedded perp exposure
captured: OI $10M-cap -> $61M -> ~$250M ATH (Jan'26); $10B cumulative notional, 2.7x faster than Pendle V2; ~0.1% of the funding pool — climbing, grounded 2026-06-12
want.sentence: Funding-exposed on-chain capital (Ethena, basis funds) had no way to trade the funding rate; Boros makes it a tradable future; adoption is visibly climbing (OI cap raised on demand within a week; $10B notional 2.7x faster than V2); blocker = liquidity (solvable); proof = OI climbing beyond ~0.1% of the funding pool.

want.name: Crypto yield-strip (Pendle PT/YT)
fit: PT/YT splitting is the native on-chain term-structure form
want.sentence: DeFi users use Pendle to split principal/yield and trade fixed vs floating; the form won on-chain; residual = breadth of underlyings; blocker = none material; proof = continued PT/YT dominance.

want.name: Rates / credit term-structure (IRS · CDX · CLO)
demand: IRS traded notional ~$249T/yr, index-credit ~$19T — but institution-resident
fit: a curve product could serve it, but the demand is institutional RV, not retail directional
captured: on-chain rates/credit-curve ~unbuilt for this demand (Maple = small inst credit)
want.sentence: Rate/credit desks use IRS/CDX/CLOs for curve & spread RV; they have ISDA netting + bank counterparties, so 24/7/self-custody doesn't move them; blocker = incumbent residency (structural, the institutional-DeFi bet); proof = a desk clearing curve RV on-chain.

want.name: Curve shape / RV (2s10s · calendar · fwd-slope)
demand: pure relative-value curve trading is TradFi-resident; ~no retail RV want
fit: expressible, but retail doesn't want curve relative-value
want.sentence: RV desks trade 2s10s/calendars; retail has no appetite for curve relative-value; the wrapper is fine, the retail want isn't; blocker = no retail RV demand (structural); proof = none expected.

want.name: Indemnity cover (P&C · cyber · life · trade-credit)
demand: global P&C premium ~$2.4T/yr — but loss-adjudicated protection
fit: indemnity pays adjudicated loss; it cannot settle as an objective binary/perp (M-gate)
want.sentence: Policyholders use insurers for indemnity cover; payout needs loss adjudication that no objective contract can replicate; the wrapper can't serve the job; blocker = M-gate (structural); proof = none — the largest gap, permanently walled.

want.name: Parametric catastrophe (weather binary · cat-loss perp)
demand: cat-bond/ILS ~$64B is INSTITUTIONAL; retail cat-binary demand thin (Kalshi weather modest)
fit: a parametric trigger is objective -> settles as a binary/perp
captured: Kalshi weather live but modest volume; cat-loss perp unbuilt — not revealing
want.sentence: Sponsors use parametric cat-bonds (institutional); a retail binary settles on the same objective trigger, BUT retail cat-binary demand is thin/novelty (legibility != demand — the depeg-cover risk); blocker = demand-reveal + liquidity; proof = a retail cat-parametric venue with sustained, non-novelty volume.

want.name: Credit-default / outage binary
demand: episodic — Polymarket bankruptcy/outage markets are thin/novelty
fit: a default/outage is a discrete objective event -> a binary fits
captured: Polymarket runs these live but episodic, small
want.sentence: Speculators occasionally want default/outage exposure; a binary fits the discrete event but demand is episodic; blocker = thin/episodic demand (hard); proof = recurring non-novelty default-binary volume.

want.name: Depeg cover (parametric, on-chain)
demand: settlement stables hold peg -> ~0 cover demand (the legibility trap)
fit: an objective peg threshold settles parametrically
captured: Cork pivoted to OTC after its exploit; the on-chain tradeable form is gone
want.sentence: The wrapper is clean (objective peg) but settlement stables don't depeg, so cover demand is ~0; salience != demand; blocker = no demand (structural); proof = none on major stables — the legibility trap.

want.name: Crypto-native protocol cover (Nexus)
demand: smart-contract / custody cover; Nexus is ~the whole on-chain supply
fit: Nexus claims-assessment is semi-subjective (M-weak); a parametric version would be native
want.sentence: Protocols/users occasionally buy smart-contract cover via Nexus; claims are semi-subjective (M-weak) and demand is thin; blocker = M-weakness + thin demand (hard); proof = a parametric crypto cover at scale.

want.name: Real-flow yield (staking · lending · LP · carry)
demand: DeFi yield — Lido/Aave/Uniswap/Ethena, tens of $B TVL
fit: these ARE the native on-chain yield forms
want.sentence: Holders earn staking/lending/LP/funding-carry natively on-chain; retail-as-the-house, captured; residual = optimization/breadth; blocker = none material; proof = continued TVL.

want.name: Tokenized cash / RWA T-bills
demand: on-chain stablecoin float ~$300B; ~$270B (USDT+USDC) earns the HOLDER ~0% while issuers keep ~5%
fit: a tokenized T-bill / yield-bearing stable faithfully delivers the underlying cash yield
captured: yield-bearing ~$25-35B (tok-Treasuries $12.9B, sUSDS $6.5B +72%/qtr, sUSDe, USDY) ~10% of float, CLIMBING
want.sentence: Holders of $270B in 0%-yield stablecoins forgo ~5%; tokenized T-bills / yield-bearing stables redirect that to the holder, on already-on-chain capital; migration is visibly climbing; blocker = distribution / compliant wrapper (solvable); proof = yield-bearing share of the float continuing to climb.

want.name: Naive underwriting vaults (vol-sell · CDS · cat DOV)
demand: looks-large (retail chases yield) but it is retail-as-the-MARK
fit: a pooled vault sells negative-skew tails to retail who can't price them -> the wrapper harms the user
want.sentence: Yield-chasers deposit into vol/CDS/cat vaults and unknowingly underwrite negative-skew tails (retail-as-AIG); the wrapper destroys the user; blocker = tail mispricing (structural); proof = none — the DOV graveyard confirms it.

want.name: Managed / structured vol-income (income-ETF analog)
demand: the ~$120B covered-call income-ETF complex proves retail wants packaged vol-income
fit: works as a MANAGED/structured product (a desk runs the tail); a naive on-chain pooled vault does not
captured: the working product is off-chain (ETFs); the on-chain managed version is ~unbuilt
want.sentence: Income investors buy covered-call ETFs for packaged vol-income; it works because a manager runs the tail; an on-chain version needs the same managed structure, not a naive vault; blocker = managed-risk structure (hard); proof = an on-chain managed vol-income product that survives a vol spike.

want.name: House-edge vault (on-chain casino bankroll)
demand: on-chain casino / house-bankroll — the one positive-edge 'be the house' product
fit: a house vault gives the depositor the positive casino edge — retail IS the house
captured: on-chain casinos + house vaults live, growing
want.sentence: Gamblers play casino games; a house vault lets depositors take the positive house edge; but US gambling regulation gates the depositor-facing product and the yield needs the casino to have players; blocker = regulation (hard); proof = a compliant house-vault with sustained positive carry.

cells.part_src: SEC, Division of Trading and Markets, Office of Analytics and Research, 'Roundtable on Options Market Structure: Supporting Data', 9 Apr 2026, Figure 10.2 and §10 — VOLUME-WEIGHTED BLEND of the two populations the SEC reports separately, because this cell covers both: Individual Customer is 73.5% on expiration day and 54.3% on non-expiry days, EX-MARKET-MAKERS, % of contract volume, Dec 2025; 0DTE is 28% of total contract volume, up from 19.6% at the start of 2022. So pro = 0.28*0.265 + 0.72*0.457 = 0.403. CAT account-type tag — a direct regulatory classification, not a size or routing proxy — and ex-market-makers is MS-39's directional base by construction.
cells.part_caveat: TWO ASSUMPTIONS, both stated rather than buried. (1) The 28% weight is a share of CONTRACT VOLUME and this pool is SPEND; per-contract cost is roughly flat across tenors (~$0.60 all-in), so the two are close, but if 0DTE carries a lower per-contract cost its spend weight is smaller and the blend rises toward 0.457. (2) The SEC figure covers all listed options — equity, ETP and index — and index skews institutional (OCC pkind: firm is 14.2% of directional flow in index against 10.6% in equity), so an equity-only figure sits BELOW this. Neither is adjusted for, because neither adjustment is measured.
cells.part_superseded: 0.55 authored, then 0.457 on 2026-07-30. The 0.457 was an error of SCOPE, not of source: it is the SEC's non-expiry row applied to a cell that includes expiry. Corrected to the blend. Classification is unchanged — unclassified either way — but the figure was wrong. Earlier candidates rejected: OCC firm-only 0.108 (its Customer bucket hides institutional customers, 21.8% of directional flow), Cboe ~0.35 (notional basis, one exchange, Q4 2023), NYSE 45% retail (a size proxy that over-captures, and it counts both sides).
cells.part_0dte_bifurcation: THE CELL AVERAGES TWO POPULATIONS THAT CLASSIFY DIFFERENTLY, and the board should say so rather than hide it. 0DTE is 26.5% professional over roughly $2.52B of this pool, which reads ACROSS (retail-reachable). Longer-dated is 45.7% over ~$6.48B, which reads unclassified. The blend reads unclassified. The pitch's named example is the 0DTE half and it IS retail-reachable on a regulator's own data — that survives being averaged, but only if someone says it out loud.

fees + commissions + spread on CME commodity futures. Calendar spreads and other curve structures are in it: a calendar spread executes as one future bought and one sold, so what is paid on it is paid on commodity futures. Curve · Commodities · Term structure is counted here, once, and so are the futures legs of Curve · Commodities · Shape, whose option legs are on Options; neither states a figure of its own (NOT-539). Not the roll cost a futures-based commodity ETF bears, which is Curve · Commodities · Carry's. Authored, not computed (NOT-538): CME and ICE publish their fees only per product line, futures and options together, and the spread term needs each product's volume and tick value, which nobody collects for either exchange, so no venue's spend is complete. What is computed, and every gap: atlas.json futuresSpend and design/data/sources/price.md §8

Price.unit: USD bn / yr of demand-side spend — commissions, spread, premium, funding and expense ratios
Price.scope: global; marked on the price level, 0:∞ — continuous price exposure only. A position marked on a probability, 0:1, is counted on the Events continent, a bet on a level included

method.spend: demand-side spend = explicit take + effective spread crossed. Book: hold. Casino: GGR. Exchange: fees + half-spread × notional. Perp: fees + half-spread + funding drag.
anchors: Regulated global sports betting GGR ~$94B (2024, H2 Gambling Capital / IBIA); ~$88B 2026 (Statista). Offshore/grey added at ~32% of online GGR.
Prediction markets ~$3B annual revenue run rate (Citizens Bank, 2026); Kalshi ~$850M 2026 fee revenue; combined ~$44.8B monthly volume (The Block / Pew, Jun 2026).
Crypto perpetuals ~$7.24T monthly volume (CoinGecko, Jan 2026); Hyperliquid 2.5bp taker.
Global iGaming GGR $115B 2026; online casino ~$60B; land-based casino ~$165B.
method.confidence: PARTICIPANT SPLITS SOURCED ON THIS BOARD carry a `part_src` on the cell: Public equity × Options at 40.3% professional (SEC Roundtable, CAT account-type, ex-market-makers, Dec 2025), and FX & rates × Options at 1% retail, because the instrument is OTC and ISDA and eligible-contract-participant requirements bar retail access. Every other split on this board is authored and marked so. Form-by-form splits inside each row are allocations, not measurements. Latent figures are arguments carrying a named detector and falsifier. MOTIVE is a categorical call on each cell, authored, never a share.
method.period: All figures are ANNUAL RUN RATE, not trailing twelve months. Captured is the latest complete quarter (Q2 2026, Apr–Jun) × 4 — trailing-12 would understate a category growing several-fold a year. Contestable and latent are sized against the published full-year window named per row below.

contestable.Crypto-native: FY2026 venue volumes × current fee schedules
contestable.Real estate: FY2026 estimate — thinnest row on the map

basis.latent: sized against the same window as the incumbent band in the same cell

method.derivation: sized from FY2026 venue volumes × published fee schedules, plus effective spread where the venue charges no explicit fee

Price.claim: FOR what is paid to hold continuous price exposure (commissions, spread, premium, funding and expense ratios), by subject and exposure. NOT a position marked on a probability, which is counted on Events. SPEND BY SUBJECT AND EXPOSURE / YR · a pool: money no other board counts · not cash traded, handle or notional.

cells.part_src: NAIC / S&P Global Market Intelligence, Exhibit of Premiums and Losses, FY2024: commercial lines are 48.4% of US direct premium written ($502.3B of $1,037.2B) against personal lines 51.6%. Corroborated independently at 46% commercial by Swiss Re sigma 3/2025 (emerging markets) and at >50% implied by McKinsey's Global Insurance Report 2025 (personal lines ~$1.1T of a ~$2.2-2.4T global pool). Three sources, none near the 0.25 this replaces.
cells.part_superseded: 0.25 authored. It was scoped to PERSONAL LINES while the pool is ALL P&C — the cell contradicted itself: `take` names ~$2.4T of P&C premium (personal AND commercial) while `src` read 'Auto and home insurers', and 0.25 is consistent with the src label rather than the pool. Both are now corrected. This is also the second 'one quantity, two homes' on this board: draft-engines-board.py already allocates P&C 50/50 from the SAME NAIC source ($260B retail / $260B pro), so the two homes disagreed 2x on the largest figure Atlas carries.
cells.part_caveat: BASIS MISMATCH, stated rather than hidden. The split is measured on PREMIUM WRITTEN; this cell's quantity is the LOAD (premium net of expected loss). No source splits load by buyer type — searched. If commercial lines run lower loss ratios than personal, their share of LOAD exceeds their share of PREMIUM and the true figure is above 0.484; the reverse if not. Direction unknown, magnitude unmeasured, so the premium split is used unadjusted as the best available proxy. It is a far better proxy than 0.25, which matches no measurement on either basis.

cells.part_src: INSTITUTIONAL BY CONSTRUCTION, like Catastrophe. The buyer of record in a pension buy-in, buyout or longevity swap is the plan sponsor or scheme trustee — never the retiree who benefits. US PRT was $51.8B in 2024 over 794 contracts (LIMRA), UK buy-in/buyout GBP47.8bn (LCP), UK longevity swaps GBP8bn over four schemes (WTW). Every one institutional.
cells.part_scope: THE DENOMINATOR, resolved from the pool size. This cell is $12.40B of load at the stated ~22% rate, implying a ~$56B premium pool — which lands on US PRT ALONE ($51.8B, within 8%), not on US+UK ($112B) and nowhere near a pool including retail annuities ($554B). BRIEFING.md independently reads it the same way, calling $56B 'the pool the board assumed' against a sourced US+UK $99B. So retail individual annuities are NOT in scope at any candidate scale — including them would multiply the pool ~10x. If the pool is ever widened to include them (US retail annuity sales were $432.4B in 2024, LIMRA), THIS SPLIT MUST MOVE WITH IT — the blend would fall to ~0.22.
cells.part_superseded: 0.612 authored. No denominator produces it: institutional-only scopes give ~1.00 and a retail-inclusive scope gives ~0.22. It sat between two answers 5x apart and matched neither. The residual 0.02 retail is a deliberate allowance for small self-administered schemes and individual buy-outs at the margin, not a measured figure.

method.kalshi: DCM bulletin cash per series, cadence from Kalshi's own `frequency`, subject from its own `category`; `custom` resolved by declared title rules
method.kalshi_priced: A Kalshi cell is stated as the cash of the series the bulletin priced when every row in it says whether the bulletin priced it, every priced row carries cash, no bulletin cash that no listed series could take can be in its subject, and the bulletin priced at least one of its series. A listed series the bulletin did not price recorded no trades it priced and is never written as $0. Any other cell is a gap and says which condition failed.
method.pm: series volume24hr, cadence from Polymarket's own `recurrence` field across 2,493 series
method.frontier: an unoccupied Daily or Intraday cell in a subject already carrying at least $1B/yr, of which at least $0.25B/yr trades slower than daily; sized at that subject's measured slower-than-daily turnover
method.unresolved_note: cash whose cadence neither venue's own labels determine. shift_12mo.pillar: 2 — where competitors expanded, and how much of it came out of Polymarket
shift_12mo.verdict: 0 CONTESTED-LOSS, 0 CONTESTED-GAIN, 0 BOTH-IN, 0 BOTH-OUT, 53 GAP. Regimes are candidates, not proof of cannibalisation; GAP comparisons are withheld.
shift_12mo.shape: Each venue's allocation is compared within its own cash basis; missing classification cannot establish a trend.
shift_12mo.measure: cell cash divided by the venue's full cash, averaged over the first and last three census months; any incomplete Kalshi month withholds its comparison; Polymarket excludes declared volume-outage months
shift_12mo.why_not_a_board: the monthly series behind these deltas is NOT the reconciled cash basis this board renders — Kalshi's month there is a week-weighted sampled daily mean. Its levels must never be drawn as bars beside Polymarket's. Only the within-venue share change survives, and that is text, not height.
shift_12mo.caveat: CONTESTED-LOSS is consistent with share being taken, but is not proof. Opposite reallocations can occur independently. Read regimes as candidates.
shift_12mo.book_growth: Kalshi 5.6x; Polymarket 1.7x. Growth uses each venue's full stated cash on its own basis. A missing Kalshi month in either endpoint withholds growth; Polymarket excludes declared volume-outage months. A share decline does not by itself show a cash decline.

frames.kalshi_method: SAMPLE-DAY RULE (operator-ratified 2026-08-09, atlas docs/architecture/plan.md section 7 decision 1): 3 Kalshi DCM bulletin days per month, the 8th, 15th, 22nd, WEEKDAY-ADJUSTED — each moved to the date within 3 days of it that falls on a fixed weekday (8th->Wednesday, 15th->Friday, 22nd->Sunday), because unadjusted they are 7 days apart and always share one weekday; every month therefore samples the same 3 distinct weekdays (2 weekday(s), 1 weekend day(s)), so month-to-month MOVEMENT is not an artefact of which weekdays were sampled; an event landing on a sample day still moves it, and the days are named below. WEEK-WEIGHTED (operator-decided 2026-10-02, the NOT-225 follow-up that ratified Wednesday, Friday and Sunday): the days are weighted to a week's composition — the 2 sample(s) (Wednesday and Friday) stand for the week's 5 weekdays and the 1 sample(s) (Sunday) for its 2 weekend days, so with every day measured the weights are Wednesday 5/14, Friday 5/14, Sunday 2/7, not 1/3 each. ASSUMPTION: Sunday stands in for Saturday, which is never sampled (as the weekday samples stand in for the weekdays not sampled), so a subject that trades on one weekend day and not the other is misread by the weekend weight. A day not published, or served but truncated or not measurable, is a GAP for that day with its reason and no other day is substituted: its weight is null and its share of the week passes to the measured days of its own class; a class with no measured day is UNREPRESENTED (week_unrepresented), the weights are renormalised over the classes that remain and the month says so; a month with no measured day is a gap record with every figure null. VOLUME-WEIGHTED MEAN: cash_usd, contracts, series_with_volume and every top[ticker] are the week-weighted mean of the measured days (day_weights), so top[t] / cash_usd is the mean of the daily shares weighted by each day's week weight times its cash; top keeps the 400 largest series, so a share over the sum of top is a share of those series and reads high by 1 / top_share_of_cash. series_with_volume is the week-weighted mean of each day's distinct series that traded, not a count across the days. THIS MONTH, 2025-10: 8th->2025-10-08 (Wednesday, +0 d) measured, weight 5/14; 15th->2025-10-17 (Friday, +2 d) measured, weight 5/14; 22nd->2025-10-19 (Sunday, -3 d) measured, weight 2/7. SAMPLE QUANTITIES, NOT MONTHLY TOTALS: $66,257,550.25 cash, 143,208,235 contracts and 1039.36 series with volume are week-weighted means per sample day over the 3 day(s) measured; never multiply them to a month or a year. Cash is ESTIMATED (contracts x traded-range midpoint; the bulletin carries no VWAP); 988,721 contracts per day have no usable price in the filing and are counted in contracts, never valued in cash_usd. 835,136 of them (84.5%) are in KXMVENFLMULTIGAMEEXTENDED, so its cash in top is a FLOOR; a share drawn from top leaves every series' unpriced contracts out of numerator and denominator alike, so its bias has no known sign. top is the 400 largest series by pooled cash and covers 99.92% of it.

ASSUMPTION: Sunday stands in for Saturday, which is never sampled (as the weekday samples stand in for the weekdays not sampled), so a subject that trades on one weekend day and not the other is misread by the weekend weight. A day not published, or served but truncated or not measurable, is a GAP for that day with its reason and no other day is substituted: its weight is null and its share of the week passes to the measured days of its own class; a class with no measured day is UNREPRESENTED (week_unrepresented), the weights are renormalised over the classes that remain and the month says so; a month with no measured day is a gap record with every figure null. VOLUME-WEIGHTED MEAN: cash_usd, contracts, series_with_volume and every top[ticker] are the week-weighted mean of the measured days (day_weights), so top[t] / cash_usd is the mean of the daily shares weighted by each day's week weight times its cash; top keeps the 400 largest series, so a share over the sum of top is a share of those series and reads high by 1 / top_share_of_cash. series_with_volume is the week-weighted mean of each day's distinct series that traded, not a count across the days. THIS MONTH, 2026-04: 8th->2026-04-08 (Wednesday, +0 d) measured, weight 5/14; 15th->2026-04-17 (Friday, +2 d) measured, weight 5/14; 22nd->2026-04-19 (Sunday, -3 d) measured, weight 2/7. SAMPLE QUANTITIES, NOT MONTHLY TOTALS: $180,968,550.93 cash, 492,831,439 contracts and 1729.36 series with volume are week-weighted means per sample day over the 3 day(s) measured; never multiply them to a month or a year. Cash is ESTIMATED (contracts x traded-range midpoint; the bulletin carries no VWAP); 39,634,057 contracts per day have no usable price in the filing and are counted in contracts, never valued in cash_usd. 19,539,033 of them (49.3%) are in KXMVESPORTSMULTIGAMEEXTENDED, so its cash in top is a FLOOR; a share drawn from top leaves every series' unpriced contracts out of numerator and denominator alike, so its bias has no known sign. top is the 400 largest series by pooled cash and covers 99.52% of it.

framesMeta.panelCap: VENUE CASH ON DIFFERENT BASES · NOT ADDABLE
framesMeta.measure: each venue's share of its full cash denominator, per subject and cadence; unclassified and truncated cash is never renormalized away
framesMeta.why_share_not_dollars: Kalshi is a week-weighted sampled daily cash mean; Polymarket is whole-life event cash attributed to resolution month. Their levels are not addable. Within-venue shares describe composition on each venue's own basis.
framesMeta.pm_basis: Gamma /events, swept by cutting time; unknown count of events over the sweep's window. Each event's whole-life cash is attributed to its resolution month.
framesMeta.pm_one_off_visible: Events with no recurring series are visible at the event grain.
framesMeta.kalshi_basis: Kalshi DCM bulletin: week-weighted sampled daily cash means, not calendar-month totals. Wednesday and Friday each carry 5/14 and Sunday 2/7 of a complete sample. Each frame keeps the producer's actual method, including gap-day reweighting. Report tickers join only through the census's top_series; subject and cadence come from the pinned semantic map.

kalshi_freshness.reason: the vendored monthly census declares no freshness as_of under a name gate/as_of.py reads; its reporting-month keys describe the observation window, not a freshness date

framesMeta.kalshi_classification: Mapped top cash is divided by full census cash, including cash outside top. Excluded mappings retain count, cash and reasons per month. Known cells are lower bounds in a partial month; absent cells are gaps. Shift comparisons with incomplete classification are withheld.
framesMeta.pm_null_volume: 149360 events in the months whose cash is stated returned a null volume and are aggregated as zero. This retains the existing sampled on-chain untraded-event assumption; it does not apply to a volume-outage month.
framesMeta.pm_volume_outage: GAP, NOT A DIP: in 2026-03, 38.4% of the open interest recorded on the events that resolved in it ($251.2M of $653.8M) sits on events that report no volume in Gamma's sweep (57,708 of 89,196 events), and 36.4% of the open interest recorded on the events that opened and resolved in it ($165.9M of $455.8M) sits on events that report no volume in Gamma's sweep (56,132 of 83,084 events), over the 25% threshold. The rule measures the open interest that sits on events reporting no volume and cannot say why Gamma did not report it, so no cash, mix or share of the month is stated and it is no end of any comparison. Not a low value
framesMeta.sampling: Latest twelve census month keys, including gaps. Kalshi uses week-weighted sampled daily means; the sample is not a calendar-month total.
framesMeta.headline: reporting window 2025-10 through 2026-09; Kalshi source freshness as_of not declared. Kalshi sampled daily cash and Polymarket resolution-month cash use separate denominators; gaps remain explicit

shiftMeta.question: where did each venue's book move over twelve months, and did they diverge
shiftMeta.measure: cell cash divided by the venue's full cash, averaged over the first and last three census months; any incomplete Kalshi month withholds its comparison; Polymarket excludes declared volume-outage months
shiftMeta.why_not_combined_share: Kalshi is a week-weighted sampled daily cash mean; Polymarket is whole-life event cash attributed to resolution month. The levels are not addable. Each mix change compares one venue's own cash basis.
shiftMeta.cannibalisation_caveat: CONTESTED-LOSS is consistent with share being taken, but is not proof. Opposite reallocations can occur independently. Read regimes as candidates.

book_growth.note: Growth uses each venue's full stated cash on its own basis. A missing Kalshi month in either endpoint withholds growth; Polymarket excludes declared volume-outage months. A share decline does not by itself show a cash decline.

segmentExpansion.question: what did Polymarket's catalogue expansion do to the professional share of its own flow
segmentExpansion.measure: implied professional share = monthly subject mix x each subject's MEASURED professional share, held fixed across the window
segmentExpansion.isolates: the MIX EFFECT alone. Blind to any change in who trades a given subject — if professionals arrived in sports this year, this series cannot see it. The number is IMPLIED, never measured.
segmentExpansion.headline: implied professional share a GAP attributed (no month carries a measured split), a GAP same-month (no month carries a measured split), as the catalogue moved into sports; no implied share for 2025-08 attributed, 2025-09 attributed, 2025-10 attributed, 2025-11 attributed, 2025-12 attributed, 2026-01 attributed, 2026-02 attributed, 2026-04 attributed, 2026-05 attributed, 2026-06 attributed, 2026-07 attributed, 2026-08 attributed, 2026-09 attributed, 2025-08 same-month, 2025-09 same-month, 2025-10 same-month, 2025-11 same-month, 2025-12 same-month, 2026-01 same-month, 2026-02 same-month, 2026-04 same-month, 2026-05 same-month, 2026-06 same-month, 2026-07 same-month, 2026-08 same-month, 2026-09 same-month: none of that cash sits in a subject with a measured professional split, so each is a GAP, not a zero; 2026-03: a GAP on both bases, not a low month. More than 25% of the month's open interest sits on events that report no volume, and the rule measures the open interest that sits on events reporting no volume and cannot say why Gamma did not report it, so no such month is an end of this comparison
segmentExpansion.why: NOT STATED: the pooled participant split is a gap (participant.json `pooled.status` 'gap'): the pool needs this run's scan and the scans retained one, two and three weeks before it, each usable; at least one of them is missing on this host or cannot be used (a scan that read too little of its window, or records nothing of how much it read, is not a week), and a shorter pool would be a different rule. participant.json's `pooled.weeks` names each and why., so no subject's split moves the implied series, and what moves it cannot be said
segmentExpansion.two_bases: ATTRIBUTED books each event's whole-life cash to its resolution month and is distorted by any large long-dated settlement — July 2026 reads 88% sports only because `world-cup-winner` settled $4,328.0M, 41% of the month, in one go. SAME-MONTH keeps only events that opened and resolved inside the month and is far closer to what traded; it drops the long-dated book, where the one-off markets live. The direction holds on both. The magnitude roughly halves on the honest one, and the honest one is same-month.

method.axis: PREDICATE: occurrence · directional · threshold · range · categorical · combinatorial · unresolved
method.combinatorial: PARLAY at Polymarket, COMBO at Kalshi — the two venues do not share a word, so the board uses Polymarket's own contract name. It replaced `conjunction`, which was logic jargon nobody in this industry says. Polymarket's figure is no longer form_map's: form_map reads market payloads tagged `parlays` and finds 0.03% of the book, while venue_spend.py reads the `polymarket-combos` source directly and measures $5.13M of spend on $239M of run-rate volume, growing 0.00x over trailing. The measured figure is placed and the row totals are untouched — the money was already inside them. IT LANDS ~14% ABOVE THE VENUE-LEVEL LINE and that gap is real, not slack: form_map puts the combo book mostly in Politics and Macro, the venue's measured subject mix weights Sports, and the board multiplies the two. Both cuts describe the same money. Neither is a per-subject measurement of it, because no source publishes one.
method.window_mismatch: DO NOT READ POLITICS ACROSS VENUES ON THIS BOARD. Row totals come from each venue's measured subject mix, and Kalshi's is a short bulletin window in late July with no election in it, annualised to a year. That is why Polymarket's politics appears to beat Kalshi's here by a wide margin. It does not; the window does. Kalshi's VENUE TOTAL is a 30-day run rate and is safe. Its SUBJECT MIX is not. See Frontier's `window_mismatch` for the dates and the fix that exists but is not yet wired.
method.why_not_sportsbook: the old axis (Moneyline/Spread/Total/Parlay/Outright/Live) is a sportsbook vocabulary. Crypto and macro event contracts have no moneyline and no spread, so half the venue book had nowhere to sit and every attempt to fill those cells was an ad-hoc regex that found something false.
method.no_scalar: everything settles binary. A bucketed band is a binary on a range; a ladder is a set of binaries.
method.coverage: form_map classifies 98.3% of Polymarket and 96.7% of Kalshi by volume; the residual is reported, never distributed
method.unresolved_subject: SUBJECT UNRESOLVED, ROW WITHHELD. form_map resolves what a contract PAYS ON for more of the book than it resolves what it is ABOUT. Where the subject is unresolved the volume is excluded from that venue's within-row form mix rather than placed — currently 0.15% of Polymarket's classified volume and 14.41% of Kalshi's. This costs no money on the board: row totals are measured by apply-venue-spend from each venue's own subject mix, and this shape supplies proportions only. It previously defaulted to CRYPTO, which inflated Kalshi's crypto shape 1.27x and put $49.1M of misattributed SPORTS PARLAY volume into Crypto x Combinatorial, where three separate readings took it for a measured crypto combo book. KALSHI'S COMBINATORIAL COLUMN IS THEREFORE A GAP ON THIS BOARD, NOT A ZERO — its combo book is real and measured at ~$29.8M of fees over 61 days, 99.99% sports by turnover, but form_map classifies 100% of it as subject 'Other' so this board cannot yet say which row it belongs in. It belongs in Sports.
method.evaluation_axis: terminal vs touch rides per cell rather than as columns, because the board's second dimension is subject. Polymarket's touch book is $5.5B against $3.6B terminal; Kalshi runs no touch product.
method.live: in-play. NOT a payoff shape — it is when you may trade. Its predicate mix is unknown because sportsbooks report in-play as its own category for booking reasons, and no source decomposes it. Held here rather than distributed.

robinhood_allocation.borrowed_mix: Robinhood's event-contract spend is measured; its SUBJECT SPLIT is not. The 10-Q reports one event-contracts line, so the rows below are KalshiEX's measured cash mix standing in for it.
robinhood_allocation.routed_to_three_venues: Event contracts are offered by Robinhood Derivatives, LLC through either KalshiEX LLC, ForecastEX, LLC or Rothera Exchange and Clearing LLC
robinhood_allocation.which_book_may_not_transfer: The three books disagree exactly where the money is: ForecastEx has 82 product self-certifications, none whose title reads as sports (18 of its titles match no subject in the title detector and are listed in the pinned file); Rothera Exchange and Clearing has 87 product self-certifications, none whose title reads as crypto. KalshiEX's mix, renormalised over this board's rows, places 99.5% of the venue total on sports and crypto, which are the two subjects the three venues differ about most, so which book is borrowed changes the answer.
robinhood_allocation.no_filings_of_its_own: Robinhood Derivatives, LLC is a registered FCM and files no product self-certifications; no CFTC org code in the corpus belongs to it. Filings displayed as "Robinhood Derivatives" are Rothera Exchange and Clearing LLC's (org_code ROTHDCM, renamed from MIAXdx on 2026-01-20 after Robinhood took a majority stake) under a display name market-intel corrected around 2026-07-27. This file reads org_code, never the display name.
robinhood_allocation.cannot_justify: All $0.624B is placed on a borrowed mix. The WHOLE venue total. Robinhood routes event contracts to three venues and no filing discloses how its customers split across them (NOT-264), so no part of this subject placement is justified by observation. Declaring only some remainder would read as though the rest had been established.
robinhood_allocation.renormalised: $0.136B of the $0.624B reaches these rows only because the borrowed mix is renormalised over the rows this board hosts: KalshiEX's own classifier leaves 18.5% of its cash Unclassified, and 3.3% sits in subjects this board has no row for. It stays on the board because every venue's capture must reconcile to its measured total (NOT-193); leaving it off would drop measured spend from every total that sums this board. It is part of what cannot be justified, not apart from it.
robinhood_allocation.one_total_every_board_that_folds_it: ONE venue total, rendered on 3 continents. Events writes this money and Engines and Projection FOLD it. Every one of them carries the same measured $0.624B, so summing `cap.rh` across the board set reads $1.872B. That $1.872B is the figure this allocation is questioned over, and it is one measured line shown 3 times rather than more money. No part of its subject placement is justified by observation, on any of them.
robinhood_allocation.the_election_contracts_this_was_filed_on: Robinhood Derivatives files no product self-certifications of its own, and the election contracts this allocation was questioned over are Rothera Exchange and Clearing's — one of the three venues Robinhood routes to, and the one it holds a majority stake in. 6 of that venue's 87 product self-certifications are politics contracts, filed as: Congressional Control Event Contract; Election Outcome Event Contract; Party Nominee Event Contract; Political Party Outcome Event Contract; Will <party> win control of the United States House of Representatives and <party> win control of the United States Senate in the <term>? Event Contract; Will Democrats win control of the United States House of Representatives and Democrats win control of the United States Senate in the 120th Congress? Event Contract. That is a reason the borrowed KalshiEX mix may not transfer: the nearest thing to a Robinhood book that exists is not the book being borrowed. It is NOT evidence for the direction this was expected to move — 78 of the same 87 certifications are Sports, so that venue's listed book is sports-dominant too, and nothing here says where its FLOW sits. A certification is a LISTING, not volume: no filing discloses how Robinhood's customers split across the three venues, so none of these counts is a share of anything and none of them says which way a flow-weighted cut would move.
robinhood_allocation.certified_books_as_of: The certification counts above were read from market-intel's CFTC filings collection as it stood at 2026-10-14T09:22:17Z and pinned in design/data/rh-routing-venues.json; a venue that has certified more since is not counted here.
robinhood_allocation.movement: Moved since the pinned record: Crypto +$0.054882B; Macro events -$0.000541B; Politics +$0.001049B; Sports -$0.055438B.

captureSeed.note: The within-row form split of measured venue capture, as this board derives it from the snapshot's row totals and form_map's shape. NOT a rendered figure: design/apply-venue-spend.py rescales it to each venue's measured spend and writes the result to cells.*.cap, which is its field alone (design/writers.json).

Events.claim: FOR what is paid to bet or trade on an event (hold, GGR, fees, spread and premium), by what makes the contract pay. NOT handle or notional. SPEND BY PAYOFF SHAPE / YR · a pool: money no other board counts · not cash traded, handle or notional.

Projection.source: DRAFT — Price map (by form) + Discrete draft (by form for assets, by rail for wagering)

cols.name: Dated / futures
cols.sub: source · own it to a date

Projection.unit: USD bn / yr of demand-side spend — commissions, spread, premium, funding and expense ratios
Projection.scope: DRAFT. Columns 1-5 are where the demand already transacts; columns 6-7 are the simplified wrappers projecting it. Asset subjects split by form; wagering subjects split by rail, because a sportsbook is the source and the exchange is the projection. Event/binary is unsourced on asset rows: those cells exist and are live, but no spend figure was ever authored for them.

method.spend: demand-side spend = explicit take + effective spread crossed. Book: hold. Casino: GGR. Exchange: fees + half-spread × notional. Perp: fees + half-spread + funding drag.
anchors: Regulated global sports betting GGR ~$94B (2024, H2 Gambling Capital / IBIA); ~$88B 2026 (Statista). Offshore/grey added at ~32% of online GGR.
Prediction markets ~$3B annual revenue run rate (Citizens Bank, 2026); Kalshi ~$850M 2026 fee revenue; combined ~$44.8B monthly volume (The Block / Pew, Jun 2026).
Crypto perpetuals ~$7.24T monthly volume (CoinGecko, Jan 2026); Hyperliquid 2.5bp taker.
Global iGaming GGR $115B 2026; online casino ~$60B; land-based casino ~$165B.
method.confidence: PARTICIPANT SPLITS HERE ARE FOLDED from the Price and Events cells beneath this board and carry no `part_src` of their own. Two sourced Price splits reach it as folded values: Public equity × Options at 40.3% professional, and FX & rates × Options at 1% retail (OTC). Every other split on this board is authored and marked so. Form-by-form splits inside each row are allocations, not measurements. Latent figures are arguments carrying a named detector and falsifier. MOTIVE is a categorical call on each cell, authored, never a share.
method.period: All figures are ANNUAL RUN RATE, not trailing twelve months. Captured is the latest complete quarter (Q2 2026, Apr–Jun) × 4 — trailing-12 would understate a category growing several-fold a year. Contestable and latent are sized against the published full-year window named per row below.

contestable.Crypto-native: FY2026 venue volumes × current fee schedules
contestable.Real estate: FY2026 estimate — thinnest row on the map

basis.latent: sized against the same window as the incumbent band in the same cell

method.derivation: sized from FY2026 venue volumes × published fee schedules, plus effective spread where the venue charges no explicit fee
method.participant_sample: Hyperliquid's participant split is a WEEKLY SAMPLE: one 7-day scan, 2026-10-04 to 2026-10-10, 87.0% of Hyperliquid's volume on core perps (the main perp DEX, crypto assets only) across 234 markets and 2,228 wallets; not pooled ("Hyperliquid's weekly runs are not pooled: hl_participant.json publishes no pooled split"); the producer's band 46.5%-95.9%

robinhood_allocation.borrowed_mix: Robinhood's event-contract spend is measured; its SUBJECT SPLIT is not. The 10-Q reports one event-contracts line, so the rows below are KalshiEX's measured cash mix standing in for it.
robinhood_allocation.routed_to_three_venues: Event contracts are offered by Robinhood Derivatives, LLC through either KalshiEX LLC, ForecastEX, LLC or Rothera Exchange and Clearing LLC
robinhood_allocation.which_book_may_not_transfer: The three books disagree exactly where the money is: ForecastEx has 82 product self-certifications, none whose title reads as sports (18 of its titles match no subject in the title detector and are listed in the pinned file); Rothera Exchange and Clearing has 87 product self-certifications, none whose title reads as crypto. KalshiEX's mix, renormalised over this board's rows, places 99.5% of the venue total on sports and crypto, which are the two subjects the three venues differ about most, so which book is borrowed changes the answer.
robinhood_allocation.no_filings_of_its_own: Robinhood Derivatives, LLC is a registered FCM and files no product self-certifications; no CFTC org code in the corpus belongs to it. Filings displayed as "Robinhood Derivatives" are Rothera Exchange and Clearing LLC's (org_code ROTHDCM, renamed from MIAXdx on 2026-01-20 after Robinhood took a majority stake) under a display name market-intel corrected around 2026-07-27. This file reads org_code, never the display name.
robinhood_allocation.cannot_justify: All $0.624B is placed on a borrowed mix. The WHOLE venue total. Robinhood routes event contracts to three venues and no filing discloses how its customers split across them (NOT-264), so no part of this subject placement is justified by observation. Declaring only some remainder would read as though the rest had been established.
robinhood_allocation.renormalised: $0.136B of the $0.624B reaches these rows only because the borrowed mix is renormalised over the rows this board hosts: KalshiEX's own classifier leaves 18.5% of its cash Unclassified, and 3.3% sits in subjects this board has no row for. It stays on the board because every venue's capture must reconcile to its measured total (NOT-193); leaving it off would drop measured spend from every total that sums this board. It is part of what cannot be justified, not apart from it.
robinhood_allocation.one_total_every_board_that_folds_it: ONE venue total, rendered on 3 continents. Events writes this money and Engines and Projection FOLD it. Every one of them carries the same measured $0.624B, so summing `cap.rh` across the board set reads $1.872B. That $1.872B is the figure this allocation is questioned over, and it is one measured line shown 3 times rather than more money. No part of its subject placement is justified by observation, on any of them.
robinhood_allocation.the_election_contracts_this_was_filed_on: Robinhood Derivatives files no product self-certifications of its own, and the election contracts this allocation was questioned over are Rothera Exchange and Clearing's — one of the three venues Robinhood routes to, and the one it holds a majority stake in. 6 of that venue's 87 product self-certifications are politics contracts, filed as: Congressional Control Event Contract; Election Outcome Event Contract; Party Nominee Event Contract; Political Party Outcome Event Contract; Will <party> win control of the United States House of Representatives and <party> win control of the United States Senate in the <term>? Event Contract; Will Democrats win control of the United States House of Representatives and Democrats win control of the United States Senate in the 120th Congress? Event Contract. That is a reason the borrowed KalshiEX mix may not transfer: the nearest thing to a Robinhood book that exists is not the book being borrowed. It is NOT evidence for the direction this was expected to move — 78 of the same 87 certifications are Sports, so that venue's listed book is sports-dominant too, and nothing here says where its FLOW sits. expansionDetectors.question: where to expand next
expansionDetectors.what_this_is: EVIDENCE FOR A BET, not a projection. Atlas can show where demand exists, who holds it, what it costs to serve and whether the holder is beatable on cost or form. It CANNOT show that any venue wins it, and pillar 3's 'why it leads to dominance' is therefore an argument the board supports and does not prove.
expansionDetectors.penetration_note: capture is counted PER SUBJECT across the seam, because Projection books event-venue capture in the `Event / binary` column and the demand in the source columns. Reading capture off the source cell alone finds zero on every row by construction, and previously reported Sports ($139.0B, 3.1% served by event venues) as untouched greenfield.
expansionDetectors.known_weakness: ACROSS and UP are sorted entirely on the participant axis, and the participant splits on INCUMBENT cells are authored rather than sourced. The direction is robust where the share is extreme and weak near the boundaries. Cells between the two thresholds are reported UNCLASSIFIED rather than forced — a detector that always fires is not a detector. Penetration is also a SUBJECT rate applied to every form beneath it, because capture is not booked by form.

Engines.settle_note: `settle` on a cell of a Cover pool is the share of that POOL's money that settles on adjudicated loss (indemnity) or on an objective trigger (parametric), read off Cover's own columns. An event contract is parametric by construction, so the indemnity share is form a venue cannot write at any size. Cells of other pools carry no `settle`: their source boards do not split money by how it settles.

method.participant_sample: Hyperliquid's participant split is a WEEKLY SAMPLE: one 7-day scan, 2026-10-04 to 2026-10-10, 87.0% of Hyperliquid's volume on core perps (the main perp DEX, crypto assets only) across 234 markets and 2,228 wallets; not pooled ("Hyperliquid's weekly runs are not pooled: hl_participant.json publishes no pooled split"); the producer's band 46.5%-95.9%; Polymarket's participant split is a WEEKLY SAMPLE: one 7-day scan, its dates undeclared, 21.9% of Polymarket's volume across 50 markets and 20,372 wallets; not pooled ("the pool needs this run's scan and the scans retained one, two and three weeks before it, each usable; at least one of them is missing on this host or cannot be used (a scan that read too little of its window, or records nothing of how much it read, is not a week), and a shorter pool would be a different rule. participant.json's `pooled.weeks` names each and why."); the producer's band 3.7%-64.9%
method.motive_calls: judgment.fold over precisely contributing source cells: agreement, mixed and absence remain categorical; motive does not allocate dollars
method.fit_note: `fit` on each cell is the join of `want[].pools` and models/penetration.py, never authored on the cell. On the 5 Cover pools this board carries, 99.87% of the money — $567.60B — is indemnity. Every one of their cells reads `Indemnity cover (P&C · cyber · life · trade-credit)` impossible on `settle.indemnity`. The parametric share, $0.757B, settles on an objective trigger (`settle.parametric`), graded native by `Credit-default / outage binary` and `Parametric catastrophe (weather binary · cat-loss perp)`; Mortality / longevity carries no want for its parametric form, a gap. So Cover's money on this board, $568.36B, is NOT A CLAIM ON an event venue's book at that size: an event contract is parametric by construction, indemnity pays adjudicated loss, and the form-addressable slice is $0.757B. Moving any of the rest means persuading a buyer to convert indemnity cover into parametric cover, accepting basis risk for objective settlement — a product-design bet, separate from capture.

robinhood_allocation.borrowed_mix: Robinhood's event-contract spend is measured; its SUBJECT SPLIT is not. The 10-Q reports one event-contracts line, so the rows below are KalshiEX's measured cash mix standing in for it.
robinhood_allocation.routed_to_three_venues: Event contracts are offered by Robinhood Derivatives, LLC through either KalshiEX LLC, ForecastEX, LLC or Rothera Exchange and Clearing LLC
robinhood_allocation.which_book_may_not_transfer: The three books disagree exactly where the money is: ForecastEx has 82 product self-certifications, none whose title reads as sports (18 of its titles match no subject in the title detector and are listed in the pinned file); Rothera Exchange and Clearing has 87 product self-certifications, none whose title reads as crypto. KalshiEX's mix, renormalised over this board's rows, places 99.5% of the venue total on sports and crypto, which are the two subjects the three venues differ about most, so which book is borrowed changes the answer.
robinhood_allocation.no_filings_of_its_own: Robinhood Derivatives, LLC is a registered FCM and files no product self-certifications; no CFTC org code in the corpus belongs to it. Filings displayed as "Robinhood Derivatives" are Rothera Exchange and Clearing LLC's (org_code ROTHDCM, renamed from MIAXdx on 2026-01-20 after Robinhood took a majority stake) under a display name market-intel corrected around 2026-07-27. This file reads org_code, never the display name.
robinhood_allocation.cannot_justify: All $0.624B is placed on a borrowed mix. The WHOLE venue total. Robinhood routes event contracts to three venues and no filing discloses how its customers split across them (NOT-264), so no part of this subject placement is justified by observation. Declaring only some remainder would read as though the rest had been established.
robinhood_allocation.renormalised: $0.136B of the $0.624B reaches these rows only because the borrowed mix is renormalised over the rows this board hosts: KalshiEX's own classifier leaves 18.5% of its cash Unclassified, and 3.3% sits in subjects this board has no row for. It stays on the board because every venue's capture must reconcile to its measured total (NOT-193); leaving it off would drop measured spend from every total that sums this board. It is part of what cannot be justified, not apart from it.
robinhood_allocation.one_total_every_board_that_folds_it: ONE venue total, rendered on 3 continents. Events writes this money and Engines and Projection FOLD it. Every one of them carries the same measured $0.624B, so summing `cap.rh` across the board set reads $1.872B. That $1.872B is the figure this allocation is questioned over, and it is one measured line shown 3 times rather than more money. No part of its subject placement is justified by observation, on any of them.
robinhood_allocation.the_election_contracts_this_was_filed_on: Robinhood Derivatives files no product self-certifications of its own, and the election contracts this allocation was questioned over are Rothera Exchange and Clearing's — one of the three venues Robinhood routes to, and the one it holds a majority stake in. 6 of that venue's 87 product self-certifications are politics contracts, filed as: Congressional Control Event Contract; Election Outcome Event Contract; Party Nominee Event Contract; Political Party Outcome Event Contract; Will <party> win control of the United States House of Representatives and <party> win control of the United States Senate in the <term>? Event Contract; Will Democrats win control of the United States House of Representatives and Democrats win control of the United States Senate in the 120th Congress? Event Contract. That is a reason the borrowed KalshiEX mix may not transfer: the nearest thing to a Robinhood book that exists is not the book being borrowed. It is NOT evidence for the direction this was expected to move — 78 of the same 87 certifications are Sports, so that venue's listed book is sports-dominant too, and nothing here says where its FLOW sits. A certification is a LISTING, not volume: no filing discloses how Robinhood's customers split across the three venues, so none of these counts is a share of anything and none of them says which way a flow-weighted cut would move.
robinhood_allocation.certified_books_as_of: The certification counts above were read from market-intel's CFTC filings collection as it stood at 2026-10-14T09:22:17Z and pinned in design/data/rh-routing-venues.json; a venue that has certified more since is not counted here.

sample.description: NAIC / S&P Global Market Intelligence, Exhibit of Premiums and Losses, FY2024: commercial lines are 48.4% of US direct premium written ($502.3B of $1,037.2B) against personal lines 51.6%. Corroborated independently at 46% commercial by Swiss Re sigma 3/2025 (emerging markets) and at >50% implied by McKinsey's Global Insurance Report 2025 (personal lines ~$1.1T of a ~$2.2-2.4T global pool). Three sources, none near the 0.25 this replaces.

sources.caveat: BASIS MISMATCH, stated rather than hidden. The split is measured on PREMIUM WRITTEN; this cell's quantity is the LOAD (premium net of expected loss). No source splits load by buyer type — searched. If commercial lines run lower loss ratios than personal, their share of LOAD exceeds their share of PREMIUM and the true figure is above 0.484; the reverse if not. Direction unknown, magnitude unmeasured, so the premium split is used unadjusted as the best available proxy. It is a far better proxy than 0.25, which matches no measurement on either basis.

sample.description: RETAIL-INACCESSIBLE BY CONSTRUCTION. This instrument is OTC and requires ISDA documentation and eligible-contract-participant status under CEA 1a(18), so a retail client cannot trade it at all. Same logical form as Cover · Catastrophe, where reinsurance cannot be bought by an individual — an access fact, not an estimate. MS-41 defines retail as a natural person below the regulatory institutional threshold; MS-39 excludes dealer and CCP intermediation from the split entirely.

sources.caveat: NOT literally zero. ECP status is available to an INDIVIDUAL with more than $10M in invested assets, so a thin retail sliver is legally possible and 0.01 is carried rather than 0. A zero would be a positive claim that the quantity IS zero; this is a claim that it is negligible and legally capped.

sample.description: SEC, Division of Trading and Markets, Office of Analytics and Research, 'Roundtable on Options Market Structure: Supporting Data', 9 Apr 2026, Figure 10.2 and §10 — VOLUME-WEIGHTED BLEND of the two populations the SEC reports separately, because this cell covers both: Individual Customer is 73.5% on expiration day and 54.3% on non-expiry days, EX-MARKET-MAKERS, % of contract volume, Dec 2025; 0DTE is 28% of total contract volume, up from 19.6% at the start of 2022. So pro = 0.28*0.265 + 0.72*0.457 = 0.403. CAT account-type tag — a direct regulatory classification, not a size or routing proxy — and ex-market-makers is MS-39's directional base by construction.

sources.caveat: TWO ASSUMPTIONS, both stated rather than buried. (1) The 28% weight is a share of CONTRACT VOLUME and this pool is SPEND; per-contract cost is roughly flat across tenors (~$0.60 all-in), so the two are close, but if 0DTE carries a lower per-contract cost its spend weight is smaller and the blend rises toward 0.457. (2) The SEC figure covers all listed options — equity, ETP and index — and index skews institutional (OCC pkind: firm is 14.2% of directional flow in index against 10.6% in equity), so an equity-only figure sits BELOW this. Neither is adjusted for, because neither adjustment is measured.

sample.description: INSTITUTIONAL BY CONSTRUCTION, like Catastrophe. The buyer of record in a pension buy-in, buyout or longevity swap is the plan sponsor or scheme trustee — never the retiree who benefits. US PRT was $51.8B in 2024 over 794 contracts (LIMRA), UK buy-in/buyout GBP47.8bn (LCP), UK longevity swaps GBP8bn over four schemes (WTW). Every one institutional.

sources.participant_scope: THE DENOMINATOR, resolved from the pool size. This cell is $12.40B of load at the stated ~22% rate, implying a ~$56B premium pool — which lands on US PRT ALONE ($51.8B, within 8%), not on US+UK ($112B) and nowhere near a pool including retail annuities ($554B). BRIEFING.md independently reads it the same way, calling $56B 'the pool the board assumed' against a sourced US+UK $99B. So retail individual annuities are NOT in scope at any candidate scale — including them would multiply the pool ~10x. If the pool is ever widened to include them (US retail annuity sales were $432.4B in 2024, LIMRA), THIS SPLIT MUST MOVE WITH IT — the blend would fall to ~0.22.

sample.description: RETAIL-INACCESSIBLE BY CONSTRUCTION. This instrument is OTC and requires ISDA documentation and eligible-contract-participant status under CEA 1a(18), so a retail client cannot trade it at all. Same logical form as Cover · Catastrophe, where reinsurance cannot be bought by an individual — an access fact, not an estimate. MS-41 defines retail as a natural person below the regulatory institutional threshold; MS-39 excludes dealer and CCP intermediation from the split entirely.

sources.caveat: NOT literally zero. ECP status is available to an INDIVIDUAL with more than $10M in invested assets, so a thin retail sliver is legally possible and 0.01 is carried rather than 0. A zero would be a positive claim that the quantity IS zero; this is a claim that it is negligible and legally capped.

sample.description: RETAIL-INACCESSIBLE BY CONSTRUCTION. This instrument is OTC and requires ISDA documentation and eligible-contract-participant status under CEA 1a(18), so a retail client cannot trade it at all. Same logical form as Cover · Catastrophe, where reinsurance cannot be bought by an individual — an access fact, not an estimate. MS-41 defines retail as a natural person below the regulatory institutional threshold; MS-39 excludes dealer and CCP intermediation from the split entirely.

sources.caveat: NOT literally zero. ECP status is available to an INDIVIDUAL with more than $10M in invested assets, so a thin retail sliver is legally possible and 0.01 is carried rather than 0. A zero would be a positive claim that the quantity IS zero; this is a claim that it is negligible and legally capped.

sample.description: RETAIL-INACCESSIBLE BY CONSTRUCTION. This instrument is OTC and requires ISDA documentation and eligible-contract-participant status under CEA 1a(18), so a retail client cannot trade it at all. Same logical form as Cover · Catastrophe, where reinsurance cannot be bought by an individual — an access fact, not an estimate. MS-41 defines retail as a natural person below the regulatory institutional threshold; MS-39 excludes dealer and CCP intermediation from the split entirely.

sources.caveat: NOT literally zero. ECP status is available to an INDIVIDUAL with more than $10M in invested assets, so a thin retail sliver is legally possible and 0.01 is carried rather than 0. A zero would be a positive claim that the quantity IS zero; this is a claim that it is negligible and legally capped.

Pillar 2 handles the cross-venue question by measuring each venue against itself.
Segments.basisLine: Polymarket cash traded, same-month basis · participant split NOT MEASURED — pooled coverage gap · no continent total: twelve per-month rows summed would be an annual figure under a per-month unit, so each row stands alone

method.pillar: 1 — how the catalogue expanded, and what it did to who trades it
method.headline: implied professional share a GAP attributed (no month carries a measured split), a GAP same-month (no month carries a measured split), as the catalogue moved into sports; no implied share for 2025-08 attributed, 2025-09 attributed, 2025-10 attributed, 2025-11 attributed, 2025-12 attributed, 2026-01 attributed, 2026-02 attributed, 2026-04 attributed, 2026-05 attributed, 2026-06 attributed, 2026-07 attributed, 2026-08 attributed, 2026-09 attributed, 2025-08 same-month, 2025-09 same-month, 2025-10 same-month, 2025-11 same-month, 2025-12 same-month, 2026-01 same-month, 2026-02 same-month, 2026-04 same-month, 2026-05 same-month, 2026-06 same-month, 2026-07 same-month, 2026-08 same-month, 2026-09 same-month: none of that cash sits in a subject with a measured professional split, so each is a GAP, not a zero; 2026-03: a GAP on both bases, not a low month. More than 25% of the month's open interest sits on events that report no volume, and the rule measures the open interest that sits on events reporting no volume and cannot say why Gamma did not report it, so no such month is an end of this comparison
method.read_it_on: the PARTICIPANT lens shows 'Split not measured'. method.basis: SAME-MONTH — events that opened and resolved inside the month. Excludes the long-dated book, which is where one-off markets live, so this understates one-off activity.

Segments.claim: FOR what Polymarket's catalogue expansion did to who trades it: the participant split by subject, month by month. NOT a comparison with Kalshi, whose cash is a week-weighted sampled daily mean on a separate basis. PM CASH BY MONTH AND SUBJECT / MO · a re-cut of Frontier: money already counted there, never added to it · not spend, and no continent total (twelve months summed would be an annual figure).

basis: annual run rate · demand-side spend = fees + spread · per-field observation windows (kalshi 30d; rate calibration 52 matched days (stale-measurement); hl spend/fees window gap/window gap (30/35d); spread 35d; notional 35d; pm withheld — Polymarket's spend is INCOMPLETE in the producer's output, so its capture here is withheld, not allocated. The producer's reason: MS-13: annualised from 21 day(s), under the 28-day floor — a window shorter than a calendar month may be published as itself and must not be multiplied to a year; rh 91d)

venueTakeRate.what_this_is: Every tracked venue's implied take rate, each carrying the quantity it was divided by. The rates within one group may be ranked against each other. The groups may not be ranked against each other, and this block does not total or average anything.
venueTakeRate.rule: implied take rate = the venue's demand-side spend divided by the volume quantity THAT VENUE publishes. The quotient is dimensionless, so the denominator is carried as a component of the figure's signature and gate/algebra.py refuses any ranking, sum or mean across two of them without a declared conversion.
venueTakeRate.counting_reason: no venue declares whether a matched trade is counted once or once per side (MS-40), so the denominators are undeclared on this component and the rates within a group are ranked without it. A venue publishing its convention settles it.
venueTakeRate.conversion_reason: no rate converts event-contract cash into perp position notional. They are different quantities, not the same quantity in different units: perp notional is a position size against a small posted margin, event cash is the money that actually changed hands. venue-spend.json states the rule for the underlying figures and a rate derived from them inherits it.
venueTakeRate.cross_group_refusal: RANK REFUSED across Hyperliquid, Kalshi, Polymarket: window differs (Kalshi = P1Y annualised from P30D; Hyperliquid, Polymarket = P1Y, observation window undeclared); denominator.quantity differs (Kalshi, Polymarket = 'cash_traded.event_contracts'; Hyperliquid = 'notional.perp_position'). These are different quantities. Declare a conversion in conversions/registry.json — the component, both sides, the rate, its source, an owner and a test — or state them separately.
venueTakeRate.notional_never_aggregated: Notional is shown per venue on that venue's OWN basis and enters no total, no mean and no ranking. atlas.json:notionalBasis declares three different quantities under one field name — face, cash traded and position notional — so there is no unit under which two of them could be added.

denominator_identification.what: fees / the denominator this repo divides by, against the effective take the producer recorded from a different pair of series
denominator_identification.establishes: WHICH denominator, not the rate. The producer's fee line was computed over this same quantity, so agreement means the two halves still refer to one quantity.

groups.undeclared_reason: no venue declares whether a matched trade is counted once or once per side (MS-40), so the denominators are undeclared on this component and the rates within a group are ranked without it. A venue publishing its convention settles it.

render.note: The display vocabulary a surface may use. It lives in the data because a renderer that decides the currency symbol, the magnitude ladder, or what an absent figure looks like has authored the unit - docs/architecture/plan.md §1 rule 2. Written by design/stamp-as-of.py.

gap.label: GAP
gap.note: no admitted figure. The reason travels with it. Never a zero: a zero is a positive claim that the quantity IS zero, which is the claim the gate declined to admit.

ungraded.label: UNGRADED
ungraded.note: the render manifest holds no entry for this figure, so nothing graded it - which is not the gate having passed it. Drawn with its number and this mark, never unmarked.

money.note: The ladder the surface prints a figure on. `atLeast` and `coarseAtLeast` are tested against the figure AS SUPPLIED, in `input` units; `multiply` takes it to the step's own suffix. A figure below the last step's `atLeast` has no step and renders as a gap.

render.boardFieldsNote: The declarations a BOARD makes about itself, read by the panel kicker, the panel footer, the legend caption, the dossier headline, the header basis line and the shared ruler (`basis`, the family id stamped from gate/export.py:ALGEBRA) and the board's one-line claim (`claim`, stamped by design/stamp-algebra.py from gate/claims.py). A field named here and absent from a board renders as a gap on that board - it is never defaulted.
